question: Which JavaScript framework is NOT primarily used for building SPAs?
answers: Vue
Express
React
Angular
correctAnswer: Express

question: Why should "state-changing" API methods (POST, PUT, DELETE) always require a CSRF token?
answers: To make the code look more complex
To track how many times a user clicks a button
Because GET requests are generally considered safe and shouldn't change data, whereas these methods modify server state
To prevent the database from filling up
correctAnswer: Because GET requests are generally considered safe and shouldn't change data, whereas these methods modify server state

question: In an SPA, what does the server usually send in response to the very first request?
answers: A raw CSV file
A complete set of all possible HTML pages
A large PDF document
A minimal HTML file, CSS, and a large JavaScript bundle
correctAnswer: A minimal HTML file, CSS, and a large JavaScript bundle

question: What is Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)?
answers: A type of virus that infects the user's OS
A way to steal passwords via a fake login page
An attack where the user's data is deleted by the server
An attack that tricks a logged-in user's browser into sending a malicious request to a web app
correctAnswer: An attack that tricks a logged-in user's browser into sending a malicious request to a web app

question: Why might a developer choose JWT (JSON Web Tokens) over Sessions for an SPA?
answers: JWT is "stateless," meaning the server doesn't need to store session data in a database
JWT only works with React
JWT is much larger than a cookie
JWT is easier to read for humans
correctAnswer: JWT is "stateless," meaning the server doesn't need to store session data in a database

question: How does an SPA handle a 404 error if the user types an invalid URL?
answers: The browser shows a built-in error
The server sends a 404 page
The website crashes
The client-side router detects the mismatch and renders a "Not Found" component
correctAnswer: The client-side router detects the mismatch and renders a "Not Found" component

question: What is the most common defense against CSRF mentioned in the context of Node/Express?
answers: Disabling all cookies
Encrypting the entire database
Forcing users to solve a CAPTCHA for every click
Using CSRF tokens that the client must include in "state-changing" requests (POST, PUT, DELETE)
correctAnswer: Using CSRF tokens that the client must include in "state-changing" requests (POST, PUT, DELETE)

question: Which of the following is a common challenge for SPAs mentioned in Chapter 16?
answers: They cannot display images
They require a special browser
They are incompatible with CSS
Search Engine Optimization (SEO) for content rendered only via JS
correctAnswer: Search Engine Optimization (SEO) for content rendered only via JS

question: What is the purpose of the HttpOnly flag on a session cookie?
answers: It prevents client-side JavaScript from accessing the cookie, reducing the risk of XSS attacks
It deletes the cookie when the browser closes
It makes the cookie work only on mobile phones
It forces the cookie to be sent over HTTP only (no HTTPS)
correctAnswer: It prevents client-side JavaScript from accessing the cookie, reducing the risk of XSS attacks

question: What is a "Preflight Request" (OPTIONS) in the context of SPA security?
answers: A request to check if the server is online
A way to download CSS before HTML
A request that clears the user's cache
A request sent by the browser to check if the server allows a cross-origin request before sending the actual data
correctAnswer: A request sent by the browser to check if the server allows a cross-origin request before sending the actual data

question: Why is an SPA potentially more vulnerable to CSRF when using session-based authentication?
answers: Because the browser automatically attaches session cookies to all API requests, even if initiated from a different site
Because SPAs don't use encryption
Because SPAs lack a backend
Because JavaScript is inherently insecure
correctAnswer: Because the browser automatically attaches session cookies to all API requests, even if initiated from a different site

question: Which browser API is primarily responsible for allowing SPAs to change the URL without a page reload?
answers: The Web Storage API
The Fetch API
The History API (pushState)
The Canvas API
correctAnswer: The History API (pushState)

question: In an SPA-Backend architecture, how is a CSRF token typically provided to the frontend?
answers: It is often sent in a cookie or as a custom header during the initial load or a login request
It is not needed if you use HTTPS
It is sent in a plain text email
It is hard-coded into the JavaScript bundle
correctAnswer: It is often sent in a cookie or as a custom header during the initial load or a login request

question: Why is "State Management" more complex in an SPA?
answers: Because the browser deletes variables frequently
Because of the file system limits
Because the app lives for a long time and must track data across many interactions
Because JavaScript doesn't support variables
correctAnswer: Because the app lives for a long time and must track data across many interactions

question: What is "Client-Side Routing" in an SPA?
answers: Routing performed by the physical router in the home
A way to speed up the internet connection
Routing handled exclusively by Nginx
Managing the URL and navigation within the browser via JavaScript
correctAnswer: Managing the URL and navigation within the browser via JavaScript

question: What is the fundamental difference between a traditional web app and a Single-Page Application (SPA)?
answers: SPAs cannot connect to databases
SPAs don't use HTML
SPAs load a single HTML page and dynamically update content without full page reloads
Traditional apps are faster
correctAnswer: SPAs load a single HTML page and dynamically update content without full page reloads

question: Why are "Loading Spinners" more common in SPAs?
answers: To make the site look busy
To indicate that data is being fetched asynchronously behind the scenes
It is a requirement of HTML5
Because SPAs are generally slower than traditional sites
correctAnswer: To indicate that data is being fetched asynchronously behind the scenes

question: Which architectural pattern is often used by SPAs to interact with the server?
answers: REST or GraphQL APIs
Direct SQL queries from the browser
FTP file transfers
SOAP XML Services
correctAnswer: REST or GraphQL APIs

question: What is the main advantage of an SPA regarding "Perceived Performance"?
answers: It works without an internet connection
It uses less RAM
The UI feels more responsive because transitions happen immediately without "white flashes"
It doesn't require a web server
correctAnswer: The UI feels more responsive because transitions happen immediately without "white flashes"

question: What is "Session Authentication" in the context of an SPA and Node.js?
answers: A way to speed up the internet connection
The server stores session data in memory or a database and tracks the user via a Session ID cookie
Storing the user's password in the browser's RAM
Authenticating the user only once per year
correctAnswer: The server stores session data in memory or a database and tracks the user via a Session ID cookie
